references.text: The description of the gold altar (altar of incense) that God gave instructions to make, which is now completed in Exodus 39:38.
Bezalel made the gold altar, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense, which are the same items mentioned here.
The recipe and instructions for the holy anointing oil (shemen hamishchah) mentioned in the verse.
The recipe for the fragrant incense (ketoret hassammim) mentioned in this verse.
The instructions for the curtain at the entrance of the tent (masak petach ha'ohel) mentioned here.
The making of the curtain for the door of the tabernacle, which is the same item mentioned in this verse.
Moses is instructed to place the gold altar before the ark of the covenant and hang up the curtain at the entrance.
The book of Hebrews describes the furnishings of the tabernacle, including the gold altar for incense, as a shadow of the heavenly sanctuary.
Revelation refers to incense on the gold altar before the throne, connecting the earthly tabernacle with the heavenly reality.
The instruction (chapter 35) is fulfilled in its execution (chapter 39), emphasizing perfect obedience.
Connects the collected materials (chapter 35) with the finished holy items (chapter 39).
God's command regarding the materials (chapter 25) is realized as completed items (chapter 39).
The gathering of materials (chapter 35) leads to the completion of the sacred utensils (chapter 39).
The command concerning the most holy items (chapter 31) is fulfilled in the final list (chapter 39).
The completion of the gold altar (chapter 39) is immediately followed by its placement in the tabernacle (chapter 40).
The detailed description of the construction (chap. 37) is confirmed as completed in the overview of finished items (chap. 39).
